source.title: Dissociable roles of prefrontal plasticity in decision making strategy and execution of habitual behavior

confidence_rationale: This is a causal double dissociation (not merely correlational): selective erasure of plasticity in an ACC-to-retrosplenial-cortex pathway altered whether behaviour transitioned to habit without changing execution level, while selective erasure of plasticity in a lateral-OFC-to-central-striatum pathway altered execution level without changing the decision-strategy transition. That is close to a direct biological analogue of MECH-480's central claim -- that 'whether a policy retains behavioural-adjustment authority' and 'how strongly a persisting policy is expressed' are separably implemented. Confidence is capped below the source-quality/mapping-fidelity average because full-text Methods/Results (exact plasticity-erasure technique, sample sizes, effect sizes, statistical tests) were not accessible -- nature.com redirected to an authentication gate and the bioRxiv HTML returned 403 Forbidden. This entry is built from the verified bioRxiv API abstract plus three independent institutional/press accounts (Kyoto University research news, EurekAlert, Neuroscience News), all of which agree on the circuit-level claim and the mouse two-stage-training paradigm but none of which report inferential statistics. A future session with journal access should re-verify against the primary Methods/Results before this entry is used to argue for anything beyond the qualitative dissociation.
failure_signatures: The abstract itself flags a puzzle this paper exists to resolve, not a limitation of its answer: habit execution level (frequency/duration) is described as 'superficially maintained despite a decline in motivational drive' during the strategy shift -- i.e. before this paper's manipulations, execution and strategy looked coupled on the surface, and the dissociation only becomes visible once each pathway's plasticity is erased independently. A reader taking only the surface behavioural trajectory (without the causal manipulation) would see execution and strategy change together and could wrongly conclude they are not separable -- this is exactly the confound MECH-480's own falsifier warns against (see what_would_answer's NON-DEGENERACY guard on floor/ceiling artifacts).

The secondary sources (Kyoto University press release, EurekAlert) explicitly decline to name the plasticity-erasure technique (optogenetic vs. chemogenetic vs. pharmacological) or report sample sizes/statistics -- this record cannot independently confirm the manipulation was single-cell-type-specific, reversible, or free of off-target circuit effects, all of which bear on how directly the paper's causal claim should be trusted.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Habit formation involves two independently-controlled processes in mice: (1) a shift in decision-making strategy from motivation-driven (goal-directed) to automatic (habitual), gated by plasticity in an ACC-to-retrosplenial-cortex pathway that weakens during the transition; and (2) the level of habit execution (frequency/duration), gated by plasticity in a lateral-OFC-to-central-striatum pathway. Selectively erasing plasticity in either pathway alters only its corresponding process, leaving the other intact -- a causal double dissociation.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-480 proposes REE's dACC-analog module (SD-032b) computes strategy authority -- whether accumulated action-outcome evidence retains control over the policy (MECH-258 precision-weighted PE, MECH-260 anti-recency bias) -- as a channel distinct from a new LOFC-analog execution-gain channel controlling how strongly a persisting policy is expressed (action-selection confidence / logit margin). The paper's ACC-RSC-vs-LOFC-striatal double dissociation is a close biological match to this whether-vs-how-strongly split: 'whether the behaviour becomes/remains habitual' maps to strategy authority, and 'how much the habit is executed' maps to execution gain.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Three gaps in the translation. (1) Circuit specificity: the paper's ACC involvement is specifically the ACC-to-retrosplenial-cortex projection, not ACC activity broadly -- SD-032b's dACC-analog is not currently scoped to a specific efferent target, so the paper constrains a narrower biological claim than what SD-032b computes. (2) Construct match: the paper's 'decision-making strategy shift' is a habit-formation transition unfolding over a fixed multi-day training window, whereas REE's strategy-authority signal is a moment-to-moment, trial-level quantity (evidence-weighted control retention). These are related but not identical timescales/constructs -- the paper evidences that the underlying SUBSTRATE can support a whether/how-strongly split, not that REE's specific trial-level authority signal behaves this way. (3) Species and readout: male mice only, and the paper's execution-level readout (behavioural frequency/duration/volume) is not identical to REE's proposed execution-gain metric (softmax logit margin / action-selection confidence) -- both are 'how strongly expressed' constructs but were not shown equivalent here.
mapping.source_context: Male mice; a purpose-built two-stage training paradigm (goal-directed training followed by ~4 days of accelerated habit-induction training) enabling within-subject tracking of the goal-directed-to-habitual transition; circuit-specific plasticity manipulation of the ACC-to-retrosplenial-cortex and lateral-OFC-to-central-striatum pathways.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality is high on venue and design (Nature Communications; causal double dissociation via pathway-specific plasticity erasure, not correlational imaging) but marked down from the 0.9+ range because this record could not verify sample sizes, exact statistics, or the specific erasure technique against the primary Methods/Results -- both nature.com and the bioRxiv HTML view were inaccessible to this session (auth redirect / 403), and the assessment rests on the bioRxiv API abstract plus press coverage. Mapping fidelity is moderate: the whether-vs-how-strongly framing lines up well conceptually, but the paper's specific circuit (ACC->RSC efferent, not dACC broadly) and timescale (multi-day habit formation, not trial-level authority) are narrower than what MECH-480/SD-032b claim computationally. Transfer risk is moderate-high: rodent circuit-lesion causal evidence for a broad architectural distinction in an RL-control system is standard-genre REE literature support, but is one inferential step removed from a direct prediction about SD-032b's specific PE-weighted authority signal or a logit-margin execution-gain metric.
